content:
- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk reversal.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +2–3% in 1–2 days), leading to overshoot; apply dampening factor for spikes > 1.5% from prior day.
- Forecast mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is > 10% above recent 18d average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30d horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 1–2% lagged sentiment-weighted adjustment to end of forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with cycle phase; align forecast to sentiment trend direction, not just magnitude.
